app.title: Spike Doctor
app.summary: A person uploads a batch of current-clamp recording files and sets the channel, the stimulus epoch, and the voltage and dV/dt thresholds for spike detection. They pick which electrophysiological features to compute, either from a short list of common ones or by searching the full feature library. The interface recomputes every sweep of every file. It shows a status summary and, for each file, raw traces, a firing-versus-current curve and a phase-plane plot, plus a combined per-sweep table. A debug view with a sweep slider and a log let the person check the spike detection, and the results are exported as CSV, a multi-sheet Excel workbook with one sheet per feature, or a PDF of the summary plots.

task.text: Extract spike and passive membrane features from every sweep of a batch of current-clamp recordings, check the detection, and export the feature tables and summary plots.

data.text: Binary recording files from a patch-clamp amplifier, each holding many sweeps of membrane voltage over time with a stepped command current. The output is a table with one row per sweep (and per spike event) per file, holding the extracted features.
data.item: a sweep of a recording: one voltage trace under one current step

stage.text: extracting features from raw patch-clamp recordings, before statistics across cells

mechanism.text: Settings and feature checkboxes in a sidebar drive a reactive computation over every file. Its results feed tabs for a status summary with per-file plot rows, a combined data table, a per-sweep debug plot chosen with a slider, and a log. Download buttons appear in the sidebar once the results are valid.

field.text: feature extraction from whole-cell current-clamp recordings in electrophysiology

workflow.name: compute per-item measures across a batch of recordings and export the tables

steps.here: Several recording files are uploaded at once with a progress bar. Files that fail to load are kept with their error, and the debug sweep slider is set to the largest sweep count.

steps.step: set the parameters the computation uses
steps.here: Numeric fields set the recording channel, the protocol epoch that holds the current step, the voltage threshold for spikes, and the minimum dV/dt.
A Basic tab has checkboxes for common features, each with a tooltip saying what it measures. An Advanced tab filters the full feature library by typed text.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each sweep's stimulus window and current step are found, the features are extracted, and capacitance is derived from tau and input resistance. Features that make no sense for a sweep are blanked, and everything recomputes when a setting changes.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A text summary gives load and analysis counts and the current settings. Each file then gets a row of raw traces, spike count against current step, and a phase plane at about twice rheobase.

steps.step: open one item in detail to check the computation
steps.here: A slider picks one sweep for every file. Its plot marks detected spike peaks, the threshold line, the baseline voltage and the stimulus window above the command current, and a log lists warnings and errors by file and sweep.
Three downloads: a flat CSV with one row per sweep, an Excel workbook with one sheet per feature (current steps as rows, files as columns), and a PDF with two files' summary plots per A4 page.

distinctive: The stimulus window and current step are read from the protocol's epoch table, and the command current is rebuilt from it when the recorded one is missing.
Spike detection uses two thresholds, a voltage threshold and a dV/dt threshold, and the debug plot draws them over the trace so the person can tune them.
The phase-plane plot automatically picks the sweep nearest twice the rheobase, which is the lowest current step that fires.
Features that depend on the stimulus are dropped for files without a stimulus, and frequency or latency values are blanked for sweeps with too few spikes.
The Excel export pivots each feature into its own sheet, with current steps as rows and files as columns, ready to compare across cells.

parts.title: File upload and analysis parameters
parts.summary: Loads a batch of recording files and holds the stimulus and spike-detection settings that every computation reads.

parts.title: Feature selection
parts.summary: Lets the person tick common features with explanatory tooltips, or search the full feature library and add any of them.

spans.first: from typing import List, Dict, Tuple

parts.title: Summary Plots
parts.summary: Shows load and analysis status, the current settings, and for each file a row of raw traces, the firing-versus-current curve and a phase-plane plot near twice rheobase.

parts.title: Detailed Results Table
parts.summary: Combines every file's per-sweep feature rows into one table showing the current step, capacitance and the selected features.

parts.title: Debug Plots
parts.summary: For one sweep picked with a slider, draws each file's voltage trace with detected spike peaks, the threshold, the baseline and the stimulus window above the command current, so the person can check the detection.

parts.title: Analysis Logs
parts.summary: Lists info, warning and error messages tagged by file and sweep from loading and analysis, with a button to clear them.

parts.title: Downloads
parts.summary: Once there are valid results, offers a flat CSV, an Excel workbook with one sheet per feature (current steps by files), and a PDF of the summary plots with two files per page.
